# CV-23 — Contract cleanup

> Branch `t/maciej/cv-23-contract-cleanup` (cut from `maciej` after the Chat v2 release) · status: built, not landed
> Migrations: `supabase/migrations/20261017130000_chat_v2_contract.sql` (the drops) and `20261017131000_chat_v2_min_build.sql` (the minimum build, applied on its own once the per-platform check is live) · both applied to the local stack (each runs cleanly over itself)

## Delivered against the row

- **Retired signatures dropped** (`DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS`): `chat_op_send(uuid, text, uuid, uuid[], boolean, uuid, text)`, `chat_op_edit(uuid, text, uuid[])`, `chat_op_react(uuid, text)`, `chat_op_mark_read(uuid, timestamptz)`, `chat_op_mark_unread(uuid, timestamptz)`, `share_op_announce(uuid, boolean)`, `chat_normalize_channel_name(text)`. `chat_op_agent_post(uuid, uuid, text, uuid)` stays: the deployed connector calls it (`moduo-mcp/modules/chat.ts`, `chat_post` and `chat_reply`).
- **The `client_id` idempotency path:** `chat_op_send` (live body, CV-16's re-cut) no longer writes `client_id`; a send is idempotent on the id the client mints. The column and `chat_messages_client_uq` stay for v1 rows.
- **`chat_workspace_enabled(ws)`** answers only for a member of that workspace (its owner or a `workspace_members` row, `chat_is_workspace_member`) or for the service role (the connector); it is false for anyone else. The plan rule itself moved to the internal `chat__workspace_enabled(ws)` (service role only), which the server's own checks call after checking membership, so nothing checks membership twice. Every caller was checked: the app's `isEnabled` (a member), `chat_op__guard` / `chat__op_guard_as` (check membership first), `chat_can_access_workspace` (the presence topic, a member), `attachments_op_begin` and `chat_emoji__may_upload` (an uploader in the workspace), `chat__key_actor` (the service role). No cron job reaches it.
- v1's `chat_messages_channel_idx` dropped (`chat_messages_stream_idx` serves the stream both ways).
- `chat_channels_name_trimmed` validated (prod had 0 untrimmed names, the orchestrator's read-only count, 2026-10-16).
- **`app_settings.min_build` = `1.0.21`**, in its own migration; it only ever raises the stored value. The check is PLAT-8's per-platform one (`applyMinBuild(minimum, current, platform)`): only a desktop build can be held back.
- The app: the v1 branches of `send` / `edit` in `runtime.chat.supabase.ts` are gone, and with them the whole `format` plumbing (`ChatBodyFormat`, the outbox's `format`, `store.send` / `edit`'s argument); `normalizeChannelName` (the client twin of the dropped SQL function, no caller) removed with its test.
- Tests moved off the dropped signatures: 12 chat SQL files, `tests/chat-plan.spec.ts` (v2 send), `tests/chat-shell.spec.ts` (`chat_op_set_announcement`).
- Drift gates: `CHAT_CHANNEL_KINDS` and `CHAT_NOTIFY_LEVELS` pinned to their CHECKs (they had none), and no later migration may re-cut either under any name; the plan-source gate reads the newest plan rule (`chat__workspace_enabled`).
- The CV-0 spike scripts (`scripts/spikes/chat/realtime-*.ts`) send through the v2 op. Every other vocabulary on the brief's list was already pinned.

## Agent's choices (deferred to by Maciej: confirmed for building, may be reconsidered)

- **`min_build` = 1.0.21** (re-checked after PLAT-8): builds from before Chat v2 are production desktop 1.0.<run> up to 1.0.20 (release run #20); 1.0.21 (run #21, 2026-10-16, `prod-app` with Chat v2) is the first that sends only v2 signatures. Since PLAT-8 every build reports the `VERSION` file (1.1.0 today, staging `-rc.N`), all above 1.0.21, and the test reads `VERSION` to keep it so. Rejected: 1.1.0 (would hold back 1.0.21, which works); 1.0.20 (still calls v1 signatures).
- **Desktop-only, by PLAT-8's check; the stamped-build gate is dropped:** PLAT-8 already makes `applyMinBuild` ignore the web app (it is whatever was last deployed and follows a different branch's `VERSION`), and dev builds now read `VERSION` too, so the "release-stamped" condition I had added says nothing more. Rejected: keeping both gates (two rules for one thing); checking the web app too (a staging or rollback web build could be locked out).
- **The minimum ships in its own migration** (orchestrator's call): it must wait for the per-platform check to be live, while the drops needn't.
- **`client_id` stays as a column with its unique index** for v1 rows; only the write stops. Rejected: dropping the index (no gain: it is partial on non-null).
- **The plan tests ask as the service role** (`test.on`, which gives the caller back), since the answer now depends on who asks; the member rule has its own section.

## Gotchas (area: supabase)

- A `Bun` / `rstest` component test whose mocked `useAuth()` returns a new `runtime` object on each call loops forever when the effect depends on `runtime` and sets external state: keep the mocked object stable.
- `bunx rstest <files>` without `run` starts watch mode and never exits in a non-interactive shell.

## For later blocks

- `chat__v1_to_v2` stays: the conversion and `chat_op_agent_post` (v1 markup from agents) use it.
- The brief's other "for CV-23" notes add behaviour and stay open: `chat__reopen` keeps `later_until`; the header count includes quiet lines; `notice__gate` runs up to three times per recipient; Catch up's "N held" polls without a Focus; `isQuietNow` has no caller; the §16 shortcut rows; `gatherExport`'s missing unit test.
- `scripts/spikes/chat/realtime-load.ts` and `realtime-columns.ts` still call v1's send (spike scripts, not run by any gate).
